edits.text: - Unstable openers (sentence-initial subordinators or adverbial frames) often leave scope unresolved; cutting after them can make the earlier fragment ambiguous about what it governs.

- Continuation heads: verbs lacking their object, prepositions without a complement, subordinators or comparative markers, quantifiers, and auxiliaries frequently need later material to complete or reverse their meaning. Treat cuts that leave such a 'continuation head' on the left as high‑contra and avoid them.

- Modifiers vs predicate integrity: do not forbid internal noun-group cuts outright. Judge whether a post‑nominal modifier is essential to identifying the noun; if preserving it would force splitting a predicate–argument or create a continuation head, prefer keeping the predicate and its arguments intact.

- Noun groups & modifiers: do not ban internal cuts outright. Ask whether a post‑nominal modifier is essential to identify the noun; if preserving it would force splitting a predicate or creating a stranded continuation head, prefer keeping the predicate and its arguments together.

Input: Whistler <SEG:?> (1.5 <SEG:?> hour <SEG:?> drive <SEG:?> from <SEG:?> Vancouver) <SEG:?> is <SEG:?> expensive <SEG:?> but <SEG:?> well-known <SEG:?> because <SEG:?> of <SEG:?> the <SEG:?> 2010 <SEG:?> Winter <SEG:?> Olympics.
Output: Whistler <SEG:86> (1.5 <SEG:64> hour <SEG:50> drive <SEG:43> from <SEG:29> Vancouver) <SEG:93> is <SEG:71> expensive <SEG:79> but <SEG:100> well-known <SEG:36> because <SEG:14> of <SEG:0> the <SEG:7> 2010 <SEG:57> Winter <SEG:21> Olympics.

Appositives and post‑nominal modifiers: if a right-side modifier is essential to identify or restrict the noun, treat cuts that drop it as unsafe. However, do not preserve a modifier when doing so would split a predicate–argument relation or leave a continuation head on the left; prefer keeping predicates with their required arguments.
